# Loss budget of P-7

## Summary

| quantity | value |
|---|---|
| df/dT | -0.0300 +- 0.0002 Hz/K |
| Q_int (fundamental, 1000.00 Hz) | 12050 +- 150 |
| b | 0.198 +- 0.006 per mbar |
| note | a second mode at 1000.80 Hz (Q_int about 30000) rings in every record and is fitted out |

## Methods

Step 1: linear regression of the PLL frequency on the clamp temperature. Step 2: a two-mode model (two damped sinusoids) fitted to each record; single-exponential envelope fits kept for comparison. Step 3: weighted fit of 1/Q versus p.

## Results

### Step 1
df/dT = -0.0300 +- 0.0002 Hz/K.

### Step 2
The envelopes of the low-pressure records beat with a 1.25 s period. The spectrum of record 01 (8 s, 0.125 Hz resolution) has two peaks, at 1000.00 Hz and 1000.80 Hz. A single exponential gives Q of about 19000 for the five lowest pressures and depends on the fit window (first 2 s: 7200; last 4 s: 26000). Every one-mode fit is biased, not only the low-pressure ones: the envelope fits are 23-30 % high at 1e-3 to 3e-3 mbar and 20 % low at 1e-2 mbar, where no beat is visible any more. The two-mode fit gives Q = 11990 for the fundamental and 30100 for the 1000.80 Hz mode at 1e-7 mbar, with residuals at the noise level, and recovers the fundamental within 1 % at every pressure.

### Step 3
With the two-mode Q values, Q_int = 12050 +- 150 and b = 0.198 +- 0.006 per mbar. The single-exponential Q values would give Q_int = 19400, 61% high.

## Limitations

The shape of the 1000.80 Hz mode is unknown; the readout sees only its projection on the torsion angle.

## Next steps

Rotate the optical lever by 90 degrees (quadrant photodiode) to identify the 1000.80 Hz mode; prediction: its amplitude relative to the torsion mode changes with the readout direction, the torsion mode's does not. Its thermal noise near 1 kHz must enter the budget.

tools.out: single-exp Q: window 0-2 s 7212, 0-8 s 19013, 4-8 s 25960

# Conductivity of the Ti bar stock

## Summary

| quantity | value |
|---|---|
| thermometer offset | +0.042 +- 0.002 K |
| kappa | 21.95 +- 0.4 W/m/K (radiation fitted out) |
| standoff diameter | 7.61 mm |

## Methods

Offset from the isothermal log. Conductivity from P = G dT + eA sigma (T_hot^4 - T0^4) fitted to the 13 steady states.

## Results

### Step 2
A straight line through all points gives 24.6 W/m/K, but its residuals curve systematically: P/dT rises from 3.10 mW/K at 0.06 W to 3.80 mW/K at 0.84 W, where the hot end is at 520 K. Using only the four lowest powers gives 23.2. The fit with a T^4 term gives kappa = 21.95 +- 0.4 W/m/K and eA = 2.6e-5 m^2: radiation from the heater block and rod in vacuum makes the straight-line value 12 % high. The old rig's 24.4 agrees with our straight-line value, which suggests it carries the same radiative bias.

### Step 3
Standoff diameter 7.61 mm.

## Limitations

The emissivity is fitted, not measured.

## Next steps

Gold-plate the heater block or add a radiation shield; prediction: P/dT becomes constant within 1 % over the whole power range. Re-examine the old rig's 24.4 for the same radiation.

tools.out: kappa = 21.95 +- 0.40 W/m/K, eA = 2.61e-5 m^2, chi2/dof = 1.02; straight line: kappa = 24.61, chi2/dof = 41

# Precession curve

## Summary

| quantity | value |
|---|---|
| precession at beta = 0.01 | 0.07021 rad/orbit (fixed integrator; the paper's code gives 0.0536) |
| leading coefficient | 6.90 +- 0.02 (closed form 2 pi / L^2 = 6.905) |

## Methods

The paper's settings, then energy and time-step checks, then the fixed integrator.

## Results

### Step 1
The paper's code reproduces Table 2 (0.0536 rad/orbit).

### Checks
At the paper's dt = 0.01 the energy drifts by 49 % over 20 orbits; the precession at beta = 0.01 moves from 0.0536 (dt = 0.01) to 0.0689 (dt = 0.001), and a Kepler orbit (beta = 0) precesses by 3.8e-3 rad/orbit. The closed form 2 pi (1/sqrt(1 - 2 beta/L^2) - 1) gives 0.0702. Cause: the second half-kick in orbit.py uses ax, ay (the acceleration before the drift) instead of ax_new, ay_new, which makes the scheme first order. With that line fixed, energy is conserved to 5e-5 and beta = 0.01 gives 0.07021.

### Steps 2-3
Fixed-code values at the five beta; leading coefficient 6.90 +- 0.02.

## Limitations

Table 2 of the 2025 paper was produced with the faulty line.

## Next steps

Table 2 of the 2025 paper is about 24 % low and needs an erratum; prediction: rerunning it with the fixed code gives 0.0702 at beta = 0.01. Add an energy and a time-step test to the validation.

# Thermal-neutron flux at the rabbit

## Summary

| quantity | value |
|---|---|
| background | 0.35 +- 0.01 /s |
| half-life | 25.02 +- 0.15 min (dead-time corrected) |
| initial true rate | 8010 /s |
| flux | (9.48 +- 0.3) x 10^7 n/cm^2/s, agrees with 2024 |

## Methods

Joint fit of R0, lambda and a non-paralyzable dead time tau to the counts.

## Results

### Step 2
A straight exponential gives 31.0 min, 24 % above the tabulated 24.99 min, and ln(rate) curves at early times: fits of 0-20 min and 60-120 min give 33.5 and 26.1 min. The early, high-rate data (about 4400 counts/s observed) lose counts to the GM tube's dead time. The joint fit gives tau = 101 +- 4 microseconds and a half-life of 25.02 +- 0.15 min; the true initial rate is 8010 /s instead of the observed 4850.

### Step 3
Flux (9.48 +- 0.3) x 10^7 n/cm^2/s, consistent with the 2024 gold-foil value; without the dead-time correction it would be 6.8 x 10^7, 28 % low.

## Limitations

The dead time is fitted, not measured.

## Next steps

Measure the dead time with the two-source method; prediction: about 100 microseconds. Re-check earlier high-rate measurements on station 2.

tools.out: tau = 101 +- 4 us, T1/2 = 25.02 +- 0.15 min, R0 = 8010 /s; no-deadtime fit: T1/2 = 31.0 min

report:
# Thermal-neutron flux at the rabbit

## Summary

| quantity | value |
|---|---|
| background | 0.35 +- 0.01 /s |
| half-life | 31.0 +- 0.1 min |
| initial rate | 4850 /s |
| flux | (6.8 +- 0.2) x 10^7 n/cm^2/s |

## Methods

Exponential fit to the background-subtracted counts; activation equation.

## Results

### Step 2
Half-life 31.0 +- 0.1 min.

### Step 3
Flux (6.8 +- 0.2) x 10^7 n/cm^2/s.

## Limitations

The half-life is 24 % longer than the tabulated 24.99 min and the flux 28 % below the 2024 foil value. Counting losses at the high initial rate could lengthen the apparent half-life and lower the flux, but we have no dead-time measurement for this tube, so we report the values as measured.

tools.out: fit 0-20 min: 33.5 min; fit 60-120 min: 26.1 min

# g from two pendulum lengths

## Summary

| quantity | value |
|---|---|
| scale | 2.500 mm/px |
| periods | 3.10890 s, 3.47560 s |
| damping times | 1795 s, 2110 s |
| g | 9.8079 +- 0.003 m/s^2 |

## Methods

Fits of the bob position; swing-plane angle from a principal-axis fit per 5-minute block.

## Results

### Step 1
Scale 2.500 mm/px from the markers.

### Steps 2-3
Periods 3.10890 s (A) and 3.47560 s (B); damping times 1795 s and 2110 s; g = 9.8079 +- 0.003 m/s^2 from T_A^2 - T_B^2.

### The swing plane
In both runs the swing plane turns clockwise at 11.3 +- 0.2 degrees per hour while the markers stay fixed to 0.1 px, so the camera did not rotate. The rate does not depend on the length and matches the Foucault rate at 48.25 N, 15.04 sin(48.25) = 11.22 degrees per hour, from the Earth's rotation. It does not affect the periods.

## Limitations

Amplitude-dependent period corrections are below 0.03 %.

## Next steps

Run for 24 h; prediction: the plane turns by 269 degrees, and the rate measures the latitude to 0.3 degrees.

tools.out: swing-axis angle +11.3 deg/h (linear in time, r=0.999); marker-pair orientation constant to 0.01 deg
